biography.education: B.A. History, University of Georgia (2002); graduate Woodward Academy (1998)
biography.background: Sixth-generation Georgian from Jackson, Butts County, GA. Former co-captain, 2002 SEC Championship-winning UGA Bulldogs football team. Oil executive and insurance entrepreneur. Early Trump backer (2016). One of 16 Georgia Republicans who signed certificates declaring Trump winner of 2020 presidential election; named 'Unindicted Co-Conspirator Individual 8' in Fulton County RICO indictment but not charged; special prosecutor ultimately declined to bring charges (September 2024).
biography.financialNote: Lent his own campaign $10 million at launch (July 2025). Family has business interests in Butts County including a proposed $10B hospital and data center development backed by Jones.

campaignWebsite.note: WebFetch unavailable; positions extracted from search snippet for issues page and corroborated by news coverage and Lt. Gov. press releases.

statedPositions.quote: completely eliminate the state income tax
statedPositions.notes: Signature campaign promise. Announced at campaign launch. Corroborated by Senate special committee plan he chairs (eliminate personal income tax by 2032, making first $50K for single filers and $100K for joint filers tax-free immediately). Jones also signed Americans for Tax Reform Taxpayer Protection Pledge (Oct 2025) — only gubernatorial candidate to do so.

statedPositions.quote: giving parents more options for their children
statedPositions.notes: Campaign website and interview both identify school choice as priority. Led passage of SB 233 (2024) creating the Georgia Promise Scholarship (voucher program). Introduced SB 446 (2026) to make Georgia's participation in federal tax-credit scholarship program permanent, preventing future governors from reversing it.

statedPositions.quote: improving education systems, giving teacher pay raises
statedPositions.notes: General values statement; specifics on pay raise amounts not found in search results.

statedPositions.quote: I'm a big law and order guy who has been tough on crime as well as promoting pay raises for men and women in law enforcement
statedPositions.notes: Explicitly pro-law enforcement; campaign pledges to strengthen penalties for sex traffickers, gang members and repeat offenders.

statedPositions.quote: he made clear he wouldn't support new limits on firearms
statedPositions.notes: Explicitly opposed to new gun restrictions. Proposed $10,000/year stipend for teachers who complete voluntary firearms training and carry guns at school. Endorsed by NRA for his 2A measures.

statedPositions.quote: stands by the abortion regulations outlined in the 'heartbeat law'... no further restrictions on abortion following the 2019 law
statedPositions.notes: Supports Georgia's 6-week abortion ban (LIFE Act, 2019). Stated at 2023 legislative agenda announcement that he does not seek additional restrictions beyond the 2019 law. However, in Feb 2026 celebrated Senate passage of 'legislation to protect children' (details in voting record below). Position warrants monitoring for any evolution.
Touts immigration enforcement as accomplishment. Campaign platform listed as fighting Trump's agenda and combating illegal immigration. No specific state-level legislative details found.

statedPositions.quote: I also believe every Georgian deserves access to the right care at the right time and in their backyard
statedPositions.notes: General access framing, not single-payer or government coverage. Approach is market-oriented: reform Certificate of Need laws to allow more rural hospital and healthcare facility construction without regulatory approval. Signaled openness to Arkansas-style Medicaid expansion (private marketplace purchasing) but has long record opposing full Medicaid expansion.

statedPositions.quote: Lt. Governor Burt Jones Prioritizes Property Tax Reform
statedPositions.notes: Supports property tax reform/reduction. Applauded Senate passage of property tax reform bill Feb 2026. No specific zoning or transit supply-side housing positions found.

statedPositions.quote: I encourage Georgia's schools to apply and join past awardees in Georgia, who have benefited from this Scholarship Program, which supports STEM-related activities in schools
statedPositions.notes: Promoted STEM scholarship application for Georgia schools.

statedPositions.quote: TPUSA Act will implement reforms to ensure and enhance the First Amendment rights of students, requiring that school students in Georgia be permitted to engage in political activities and expression before, during, and after the school day
statedPositions.notes: Named after Turning Point USA. Framed as First Amendment student rights. Critics note this is associated with right-wing student organizing.

statedPositions.quote: maintaining Georgia's ban on transgender girls in girls' sports
statedPositions.notes: Led Senate Bill 1 (the Riley Gaines Act) in 2025 banning transgender student-athletes from women's sports and requiring separate restrooms/locker rooms based on birth sex. Georgia joined 26 other states with this restriction.

statedPositions.quote: Massive Burt Jones-backed project among wave of data centers proposed for Georgia
statedPositions.notes: Jones backed a $10B development in Butts County (his hometown) that includes a hospital and 11 million sq ft of data centers on land owned by his father. AG Chris Carr accused Jones of using his office to enrich family. Jones' income tax elimination plan initially included eliminating data center tax breaks to fund the rate cuts — potential conflict of interest flagged by AJC.

votingRecord.note: State legislative record is as a senator (2013-2023). Since 2023, Jones presides over the Senate as Lt. Governor and shapes the agenda but does not cast votes on legislation. Lt. Gov. press releases track his positions on bills he champions.

keyVotes.notes: Voted to establish flat income tax rate during Senate tenure. Now wants to eliminate the income tax entirely.

keyVotes.bill: Prohibition on teaching systemic racism in schools (CRT-adjacent legislation)
keyVotes.notes: Voted to prohibit teaching about systemic racism in Georgia schools during Senate tenure.
Co-sponsored legislation allowing biblical classes to be taught in high school curriculum.
Created 5-year mandatory minimums for gang offenses and 10-year minimums for recruiting minors into gangs. Pro-punishment, anti-rehabilitation policy.
Expanded cash bail requirements to 30 additional offenses including 18 misdemeanors. More punitive/less reform-oriented approach.

keyVotes.bill: Austin's Law (2024) — overdose death prosecution tool
keyVotes.notes: Gave prosecutors tools to address overdose deaths. Followed in 2025 by increasing mandatory minimums for fentanyl traffickers. Campaign promises death penalty for fentanyl dealers.
Created Georgia's school voucher program — described as 'most significant school choice victory in state history.' Strong poleB (school choice) signal.
Banned transgender student-athletes from women's sports; mandated separate restrooms/locker rooms by birth sex.

keyVotes.bill: HB 1018 / Georgia Firearms Industry Nondiscrimination Act (2024)
keyVotes.notes: Prohibited financial institutions from categorizing firearms retailers with special merchant codes; protects gun purchaser privacy. NRA praised Jones for this support.
Proposed $10,000/year for teachers who voluntarily take firearms training and carry guns at school. Explicitly opposed to new gun restrictions alongside this proposal.
Loosened CON rules so counties under 50K residents can build hospitals without state certification. Market-oriented approach to healthcare access.
Authorized up to $500 one-time refunds per household. Rate cut to 5.19%.
Supported property tax reform legislation during 2026 session.
Celebrated Senate passage of two income tax proposals described as 'largest income tax cut in state history.' Personal income tax elimination roadmap to 2032.

keyVotes.bill: SB 446 (2026) — permanent federal scholarship program participation
keyVotes.notes: Would permanently lock Georgia into federal tax-credit scholarship program, preventing future governor from withdrawing.

evidenceSummary.notes: Jones has a 10-year Georgia Senate record (2013-2023) plus 3 years as Lt. Governor (2023-present). The Senate record is voting-based; the Lt. Gov. record is agenda/championing-based (he presides but does not cast votes). Combined, this provides substantial evidence for most axes. Primary gaps are climate/environment where he has not staked out public positions (likely consistent with Trump-aligned skepticism but not documented). The fake elector controversy and ongoing data center conflict-of-interest allegations are relevant political context but do not directly affect axis scoring. Medicaid expansion positioning appears opportunistic — weight the long Senate record of opposition over recent rhetorical openness.
